Thanks for the help, I appreciate that. IIRC I joined just around the end of 4.3, but I spent a lot of time learning other stuff. So I can really only confidently state that it's been an issue on 4.4. 

As for 4.5, I kind of skirted around the issue by focusing on sprite animations so now my whole game is kind of committed to an animation system that explicitly avoids skeletons. I'm mostly here reporting bugs for the sake of community spirit. Would be amazing to see how advanced animation in Godot works for future projects, but as of now I figured out a workaround.

> But sometimes in this selection process the animation player will randomly unselect itself, the keys will disappear, and then you need to re-select the animation player at which point the skeleton resets and all your progress gets wiped.

The animation resets to the first frame of the track when you select the `AnimationPlayer` again. You have to insert keyframes so you don't lose progress. 2D has a convenient auto-keying feature that inserts keys when you make changes, but this is not implemented for 3D.

Also, when you run the project, the editor can automatically switch to the Debugger panel. You may be tempted to reselect the animation player node to open the Animation tab again, which will reset unkeyed changes. You can disable this auto-switch behavior with the editor setting `debugger/auto_switch_to_stack_trace` or just click the Animation tab at the bottom instead of the `AnimationPlayer` node, so it doesn't reset.

In the end, unkeyed changes can be lost at any time, so don't forget to insert keyframes. This is a universal issue with animation software. I always forget too..
This probably classifies more as an enhancement than a bug since there isn't a direct solution, and probably requires some discussion around how to address, so I have retagged it

I'm actually back after having done testing, and it is in fact a bug. I now found the reproduction pattern: 

1. Select animation player
2. Select skeleton
3. Animate skeleton
4. Click anything in the animation track section, maybe tweak or adjust something.
5. BOOM! Deselected. If you want to adjust a keyframe or fix your work in the very animationplayer you're working on, then it'll break whatever you're working on. 

And that to me sounds like a bug. If I am working on the very same animationplayer that I have selected, why would it suddenly be unselected? Classic case of bug. 

And the fix is simple (conceptually that is):
If you alter keyframes, keep the animationplayer active/selected, and interpolate the changes in the viewport. That way you can animate with more precision and ease and actually see what you're doing without forced iteration that wipes out sometimes hours
of work.
